title: Committee of supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: Singapore independence and defence history
sections.summary: Singapore's turbulent path to independence, National Service from 1967, SAF's growth, and eroded multilateralism, citing Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore had a turbulent journey to Independence, with our pioneer generation of leaders living through both World War II, and at the cusp of independence, the Konfrontasi between Indonesia and Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We started National Service in 1967 and over the years, have slowly and steadily built the SAF into a strong and credible defence force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: An important reason for our peaceful environment was the commitment of the major world powers to peaceful co-existence in accordance with the UN Charter for the last eight decades or so since World War II.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, the commitment to multi-lateralism has eroded over time and one recent example would be Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February last year.

sections.label: Update on global regional trends
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for Defence for an update on global and regional trends MINDEF and SAF monitor and how they are affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence therefore provide an update on the major global and regional trends that MINDEF and SAF are closely monitoring, and how MINDEF and SAF will be affected by these trends?

sections.label: Ukraine war implications for Singapore
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for Defence to comment on the Ukraine war's implications for Singapore's security and key lessons learnt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence therefore comment on the implications of the war in Ukraine for Singapore’s security, as well as the key lessons learnt from the war for us?

sections.label: UNHCR Ukraine civilian casualty figures
sections.summary: States lower UNHCR estimates: over 8,006 killed, 13,287 injured, 7.6 million refugees and almost 8 million internally displaced in Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Even by the lower UNHCR estimates, confirmed civilian casualties number over 8,006 killed, 13,287 injured, 7.6 million refugees and, almost 8 million internally displaced in Ukraine.

sections.label: SAF transformation and defence manpower
sections.summary: Notes shrinking population, defence manpower impact, rising regional defence spending, and asks for an update on plans and priorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As we continue to transform our SAF, we must be cognisant of the challenges of a shrinking population and its impact on our defence manpower, increase global spending on defence, especially in the region, and the need to maintain confidence and trust in the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, I ask the Ministry for an update on the plans and priorities that we have put in place in light of the changes in the global order.

sections.label: Singapore's need for open routes
sections.summary: States that as a commerce-dependent island, Singapore needs open use of sea lanes, submarine cables and air routes linking it to partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As a commerce-dependent island, Singapore needs open use of sea lanes, submarine cables and air routes that link us to partners in all of East Asia, across Southeast Asia, South Asia and points West.

sections.label: Straits of Singapore trade impact
sections.summary: Disruption could affect trade, communication, food and energy imports, shipping through the Straits of Singapore, and regional air traffic, with consequences for Singapore's prosperity, stability and survival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This could also affect trade and communication and even the import of food and energy, not to mention safe passage for the shipping trade and maritime traffic passing through the straits of Singapore going both east and westwards, to near and far shores for which we are so heavily dependent on and possibly also civilian and commercial air traffic in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This may prove consequential for not just Singapore's prosperity, but possibly even stability and survival.

sections.label: Defence budgets after Ukraine invasion
sections.summary: Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine, many countries have allocated bigger shares of their budgets to defence, with Germany intending to raise defence spending by at least 2% of its GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, since the Russian invasion of Ukraine, many countries have started to allocate a bigger share of their budgets to defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Germany intends to raise its defence spending by at least 2% of its GDP.

sections.label: Military expenditure single-lined item
sections.summary: In the FY 2023/2024 revenue on expenditure estimates, military expenditure is a single-lined item of $17.0 billion with no further breakdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the revenue on expenditure estimates for FY 2023/2024, military expenditure is just a single-lined item with an amount of $17.0 billion, without any further breakdown.

sections.label: Scrutiny of MINDEF budget
sections.summary: The speaker supports a strong SAF and believes more thorough scrutiny of MINDEF's budget will maintain public confidence that the $17.97 billion allocated, the highest among Ministries, goes entirely to its mission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I support the need to maintain a strong and credible SAF to effectively defend Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is why I believe that more thorough scrutiny of MINDEF's budget and expenditure will help maintain public confidence that the $17.97 billion allocated to the Ministry, the highest among all the Ministries, is going entirely towards achieving its mission.

sections.label: SAF capabilities by 2040
sections.summary: By 2040 the SAF will acquire new capabilities and assets including Next Generation Infantry Battalions, armoured tracked carriers, Howitzers, Multi-Role Combat Vessels, Invincible-class submarines, unmanned vessels, F-15SG and F-35 fighter jets, and Next Generation Unmanned Aerial Vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: By 2040, SAF will acquire new capabilities and assets, where we will have, then will include Next Generation Infantry Battalions, new armoured tracked carriers and Howitzers for the Army, Multi-Role Combat Vessels, Invincible-class submarines, and unmanned vessels for the Navy, as well as F-15SG and F-35 fighter jets and Next Generation Unmanned Aerial Vehicles for the Air Force.

sections.label: Ukraine attack as wake-up call
sections.summary: The attack on Ukraine was a wake-up call that peace and stability should never be taken for granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Chairman, the attack on Ukraine was a wake-up call that we should never take peace and stability for granted.

sections.label: Threats from all sources
sections.summary: Singapore must be prepared for threats from all sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singapore must be prepared for threats from all sources.

sections.label: Low fertility rate and NSmen
sections.summary: Low fertility rate affects future number of NSmen, so SAF would adapt through technology or policy changes, leading to transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One of the biggest challenges is our low fertility rate which affects the future number of NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: SAF would have to adapt through technology utilisation or policy changes, leading to further transformation.

sections.label: Formation progress since October 2022
sections.summary: A formation formally began on 28 Oct 2022, with parts functioning before that, and the Minister is asked about progress since its formation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With its formal beginning just three months ago on 28 Oct 2022, but with different parts of it already functioning before that, I would like to ask the Minister how has the progress been since its formation?

sections.label: AI, robotics and military threats
sections.summary: The Minister for Defence is asked for views on emerging military threats from AI, robotics and autonomous platforms, and how MINDEF/SAF will stay ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: With the private sector leading much of the technological innovation today, key technologies with high disruptive and dual-use potential are in the fields of AI, robotics and autonomous platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence provide views on the emerging slate of military threats that MINDEF/SAF will need to guard against, and how MINDEF/SAF will stay ahead of these threats?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict appears to have spurred the adoption of new technologies and we see drones being used with lethal force.

sections.label: SAF adoption of unmanned technologies
sections.summary: Unmanned technologies were identified as a focal point, and the Minister for Defence is asked about SAF's adoption of emerging military technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Of these new assets and capabilities, unmanned technologies were identified as a focal point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I would therefore like to seek views from the Minister for Defence on the SAF’s adoption of emerging and cutting-edge military technologies, and whether this would help it to remain agile and capable in responding to the range of threats.

sections.label: Singapore affected by global changes
sections.summary: Singapore, whose external trade is three and a half times GDP, is dependent on free flow of goods, services, capital and people, so these changes will affect it strongly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For Singapore, whose external trade is three and a half times our GDP, the proverbial “shop in the MRT station”, the “canary in the mine of globalisation”, so dependent on free flow of goods and services, capital and people, these changes are bound to affect us, and our country will feel the effects strongly.

sections.label: South China Sea shipping
sections.summary: A third of global shipping passes through the South China Sea and the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, carrying 80% of oil to Northeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: A third of global shipping goes through the South China Sea and the Straits of Malacca and Singapore and carries 80% of the oil transported to Northeast Asia.

sections.label: Free trade under stress
sections.summary: Post-World War II constructs of increasing free trade and open borders are under severe stress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In sum, the post-World War II constructs of increasing free trade and open borders are under severe stress.

sections.label: EU defence and conscription
sections.summary: EU countries pledged more defence spending over Russia's war on Ukraine, with some reintroducing conscription and others mulling national service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: European Union (EU) countries have now pledged to spend more on defence in the face of Russia’s war on Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Some, like Latvia, are also reintroducing conscription while others like Germany, Sweden, Poland and France continue to mull over the reinstatement of some form of national service.

sections.label: China and Japan defence spending
sections.summary: China is estimated to spend over US$270 billion with a 7.1% increase, while Japan plans to double defence spending to 2% of GDP by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: China is estimated to spend in excess of US$270 billion and announced a 7.1% increase last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Japan has announced plans to double its defence spending to 2% of GDP by 2027 and to develop counter-strike capabilities.

sections.label: South Korea defence spending
sections.summary: South Korea wants to raise defence spending by an annual average of 6.8% over five years, focusing on countering North Korea.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: South Korea wants to increase defence spending by an annual average of 6.8% over the next five years, with a focus on securing capabilities to counter North Korea.

sections.label: Defence spending growth comparison
sections.summary: Between 1999 and 2021, EU defence spending rose 20%, versus 70% for the US, 300% for Russia and 600% for China.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Between 1999 and 2021, the defence spending by EU increased only by 20%, compared to the US that went up by 70%, Russia by 300% and China by 600%.

sections.label: Doomsday Clock moves closer
sections.summary: The Doomsday Clock moved 90 seconds closer to midnight this year, the closest since 1947.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Well, this Doomsday Clock has moved 90 seconds closer to midnight this year, the closest to global catastrophe since 1947, post-World War II.

sections.label: Ministry expenditure projection increase
sections.summary: The Ministry projects expenditure of just under $18 billion in the coming financial year, a 5.6% increase from FY2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In the coming financial year, my Ministry projects an expenditure of just under $18 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This translates to an increase of 5.6% from FY2022 due to mainly three reasons.

sections.label: Defence Budget growth targets
sections.summary: MINDEF kept Defence Budget growth in line with inflation at about 4.3% yearly and expects 3% to 4% growth next decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I will elaborate on them in the response to your questions on the Digital and Intelligence Service (DIS).

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I had informed Members previously that MINDEF will strive to keep the growth of our Defence Budget to be in line with inflation and we have achieved this target for the past decade at about 4.3% each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We expect this to continue for the next decade too, to stabilise at a 3% to 4% year-on-year growth.

sections.label: MINDEF spending share of GDP
sections.summary: MINDEF's spending has stabilised at between 3% and 4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Overall, MINDEF's spending has stabilised at between 3% and 4% of our GDP.

sections.label: Second tranche F-35B acquisition
sections.summary: MINDEF will acquire eight more F-35Bs by the end of the decade, supporting F-16 drawdown and an F-35 and F-15 fleet.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: MINDEF will therefore proceed to exercise the option to acquire a second tranche of F-35Bs – eight of them – and they will be added to our fleet by the end of the decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This acquisition will support the progressive drawdown of our ageing F-16s, which will retire from mid-2030s, which means that at steady state, our RSAF will operate F-35 and F-15 fighter planes – the most advanced in the region.

sections.label: Four submarines operational
sections.summary: By the end of this decade, all four submarines will be operational around Singapore waters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: By the end of this decade, all four submarines will be operational around Singapore waters.

sections.label: NSF scheme sign-ups
sections.summary: More than 350 NSFs have signed on since the launch of both schemes, with a 40% increase in applications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Since the launch of both schemes, more than 350 NSFs have signed on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We also saw a 40% increase in applications.

sections.label: Unmanned Navy vessels
sections.summary: The Navy will shift to a future force structure where about half of its vessels will be unmanned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Navy will shift towards a future force structure where about half of its vessels will be unmanned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Fifty percent of our future Navy will be unmanned.

sections.label: Phase 1 new buildings
sections.summary: Phase 1 will be completed next year with over 60 new buildings, including a bus interchange and an underground MRT station.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Phase 1 will be completed next year and will consist of over 60 new buildings – a mix of high-rise interconnected buildings, low-rise residences, a bus interchange and even an underground MRT station.

sections.label: Murai Urban Battle Circuit readiness
sections.summary: Murai Urban Battle Circuit will be ready this year, the other two by early 2024, with up to 22,000 soldiers using them yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The first – Murai Urban Battle Circuit – will be ready by this year, and the other two will be ready by early 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: When these iBACs start, up to 22,000 active and NS soldiers will use them every year.

sections.label: Defence of Singapore commitment
sections.summary: Overseas training has limits, and Singapore must not depend on others, requiring a strong SAF and long-term commitment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Yes, we will do as much as we can overseas, but there is a limit and we must never be so dependent on others that if we have another pandemic, we find that we cannot train and we are operationally less ready.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the defence of Singapore is a long-term commitment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The success of it is not for the faint-hearted and can only be achieved if we as one people have that staying power, never flagging in spirit or effort; never lulled or deceived that Singapore does not need a strong SAF because the world is safe or that others will protect us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have come far as a multiracial and multi-religious nation to build an SAF that will fight with one heart and aim – to protect our Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We will go even further as long as we commit each year to stay the course.

sections.label: SAFTI City construction delay
sections.summary: MINDEF started SAFTI City in 2019, but the COVID-19 pandemic delayed its development, like other construction projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Back in 2019, the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) started construction on Singapore Armed Forces Training Institute (SAFTI) City, a state-of-the-art urban training facility that aims to leverage on technology to enhance training for our Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) soldiers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, due to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, MINDEF announced that the development of the SAFTI City project had been delayed, similar to other construction projects throughout Singapore.

sections.label: Shoalwater Bay Training Area expansion
sections.summary: The Shoalwater Bay Training Area in Australia is undergoing expansion and would eventually provide an area ten times the size of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One of the biggest overseas training areas we have is the Shoalwater Bay Training Area in Australia, which is currently undergoing an expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: During the Minister for Defence's visit to the troops participating in Exercise Trident and Exercise Wallaby in Australia in September 2022, he stated that the expanded training area would eventually provide an area ten times the size of Singapore for our soldiers to train.

sections.label: SAF technology, facilities, safety protocols
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for Defence how SAF uses technology, facilities and safety protocols to prepare soldiers for contingencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can the Minister for Defence share how SAF is utilising the latest technology, combine with the right facilities and safety protocol, to prepare our soldiers for any contingencies?

sections.label: Multilateral cooperation against digital threats
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for Defence for views on what Singapore can do to keep multilateral cooperation strong against transnational digital threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In order to combat these common challenges, deeper international and multilateral cooperation can be essential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In light of this, could the Minister for Defence provide views on what Singapore can do to ensure that multilateral cooperation remains strong, to address the increasingly transnational nature of the digital threats that we face?

sections.label: MINDEF regional security dialogue update
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for Defence for an update on MINDEF's efforts to foster security dialogue in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence provide an update on MINDEF's efforts to foster security dialogue in the region?

sections.label: SAF safety in realistic training
sections.summary: The passage asks MINDEF for an update on how the SAF upholds safety in training while seeking realistic and effective training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide an update on how the SAF upholds safety in training, even as it seeks to conduct realistic and effective training?

sections.label: Optimising NSmen development and deployment
sections.summary: The passage asks how MINDEF and SAF optimise the development and deployment of NSmen to maximise their skills, physical status, capabilities and contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With that in mind, how is MINDEF and SAF working to ensure that we optimise the development and deployment of our NSmen within the SAF, to tap on and maximise their skills, physical status, capabilities and contributions?

sections.label: SAF functional assessments for NSFs
sections.summary: Heng Chee How said the SAF implemented functional assessments for NSFs and would extend them to pre-enlistees with orthopaedic conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the COS debate last year, Senior Minister of State for Defence Mr Heng Chee How shared with the House that the SAF had successfully implemented functional assessments for NSFs, with more NSmen safely deployed as transport operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: He also shared that functional assessments would also be extended to pre-enlistees with orthopaedic conditions.

sections.label: MINDEF Work-Learn Schemes expansion
sections.summary: MINDEF expanded functional assessments since 2018, and Heng Chee How said the SAF will introduce two more Work-Learn Schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Since it was introduced in 2018, MINDEF had expanded it to cover more roles and vocations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last year, Senior Minister of State Mr Heng Chee How highlighted and updated that the SAF will introduce another two Work-Learn Schemes – the Digital Work-Learn Scheme for eligible servicemen to pursue undergraduate degrees in areas, such as Computer Engineering and Data Science, as well as the Work-Study Diploma for Supply Supervisors.

sections.label: Expertise-based redeployments increase
sections.summary: The speaker was heartened to hear that expertise-based redeployments rose significantly in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Chairman, I was heartened to hear last year that the number of expertise-based redeployments had gone up significantly in 2022.

sections.label: OneNS platform feedback request
sections.summary: OneNS was rolled out in the second half of last year, and MINDEF is asked to share user feedback and assess its impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: OneNS was rolled out in the second half of last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Would MINDEF share the feedback and experience from its users and assess how much difference this platform has made to the NS experience?

sections.label: Update on activities response
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked to update how Singaporeans responded to these activities and whether they achieved their objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide an update on how Singaporeans have responded to these activities and whether these activities had achieved its objectives?

sections.label: Appreciation for NSmen contributions
sections.summary: MINDEF and the SAF are asked what they are doing to ensure NSmen continue to feel appreciated for their contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What are MINDEF and the SAF doing to ensure that our NSmen continue to feel appreciated for their contributions to our national defence?

sections.label: MINDEF review timing update
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked whether a review is timely this year, four years after the last announcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Could MINDEF provide an update on whether a review is timely this year, given that four years have passed since the last announcement?

sections.label: Total Defence Ukraine takeaways
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked to share key Total Defence takeaways from the Russia-Ukraine conflict for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In light of these developments in Ukraine, could MINDEF share the key Total Defence takeaways from the Russia-Ukraine conflict for Singapore?

sections.label: Community resilience Total Defence initiatives
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked for updates on how it has bolstered community resilience through Total Defence initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I imagine that any crisis that hits Singapore shores, from either traditional or emerging threats, would demand a similar type of collective resilience, in order for us to bounce back stronger after each crisis.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, may I ask MINDEF for updates on how MINDEF has bolstered community resilience through various initiatives under the Total Defence umbrella.

sections.label: Digital Defence sixth pillar
sections.summary: The addition of Digital Defence is timely and forms the sixth pillar of Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The addition of Digital Defence is timely, which forms the sixth pillar of Total Defence.

sections.label: Civic preparedness with other agencies
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked how it works with other agencies to enhance Singaporeans' civic preparedness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: His organisation has reportedly trained more than 50,000 Ukrainians with the skills needed to render first aid, which has been particularly useful amidst the current hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: How is MINDEF working with other agencies to enhance Singaporeans' civic preparedness?

sections.label: Preparing Singaporeans for future crises
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked what it has done and will do to prepare Singaporeans for future crises and collaborate with others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What has MINDEF done, and will do, to better prepare Singaporeans for future crises?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will it muster the strong resources it has and collaborate and align with other Government Ministries, ground agencies and volunteers, to ensure that we can band together during tough times?

sections.label: ACCORD initiatives update request
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked to provide an update on recent initiatives ACCORD has been working on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would MINDEF provide an update on the various initiatives that ACCORD has been working on recently?

sections.label: ACCORD initiatives and NS support
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked to update the House on ACCORD's initiatives and how it encouraged community support for defence, particularly NS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could MINDEF thus update the House on ACCORD's initiatives and how it has encouraged community support for defence issues, particularly, with regards to NS?

sections.label: Revamping military museums appeal
sections.summary: The question asks whether there are upcoming plans to revamp these military museums to enhance their appeal to the younger generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Are there any upcoming plans to revamp these military museums to enhance their appeal to our younger generation?

sections.label: ADMM agrees to establish ACICE
sections.summary: Dr Ng updated the House last year that the ADMM had agreed to establish the ACICE in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As Dr Ng had updated the House last year, the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) had agreed to establish the ADMM Cybersecurity and Information Centre of Excellence (ACICE) in Singapore.

sections.label: ACICE construction and launch timing
sections.summary: Construction of ACICE's physical centre is underway, with a formal launch expected in the third quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The construction of ACICE's physical centre is also underway and we expect a formal launch in the third quarter of this year.

sections.label: SLD22 and 20th SLD edition
sections.summary: SLD22 was well-attended by 37 ministerial-level delegates, and the 20th SLD will be commemorated this year with Anthony Albanese giving the keynote address.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: SLD22 was a successful event that was well-attended by 37 ministerial-level delegates, including from both the US and China.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The SLD remains the premier defence and security conference in Asia and provides a venue to affirm mutually beneficial principles and to allow for dialogue, if not build trust.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We look forward to commemorating the 20th edition of the SLD this year, where Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has agreed to give the keynote address.

sections.label: Survey on NS necessity
sections.summary: A MINDEF survey found over 98% of respondents said NS was necessary for Singapore's security now and in future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In one of MINDEF's surveys conducted among Singaporeans late last year, more than 98% of the respondents said that NS was necessary for Singapore's security, both now and in the future.

sections.label: Pre-enlistee functional assessments
sections.summary: 100 pre-enlistees with orthopaedic conditions underwent functional assessments, and 75 were found fit for wider operational roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: To date, 100 pre-enlistees with certain orthopaedic conditions have undergone such functional assessments and 75 have been found to be fit to be deployed to a wider range of operational roles than before.

sections.label: Redesigned SAF jobs
sections.summary: Since 2021 the SAF redesigned 1,300 jobs for more servicemen, with 500 more jobs targeted by mid-year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Since 2021, the SAF has redesigned 1,300 jobs in vocations, such as Medics, Infantry Carrier Vehicle Operators and Transport Operators, opening them up to more servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: The SAF is on track to do the same for another 500 jobs by the middle of this year, and that will bring it from 1,300, to 1,800 jobs.

sections.label: NSF Work-Learn Scheme enrolment
sections.summary: 450 NSFs have enrolled in Work-Learn Schemes so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Overall, 450 NSFs have enrolled in such Work-Learn Schemes so far.

sections.label: Redeployment of NSmen
sections.summary: Over the past year the SAF redeployed 200 NSmen under the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Over the past year, the SAF has redeployed 200 NSmen under the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

sections.label: Digital NS recognition credits
sections.summary: Since 2021 cash and voucher-based NS recognition benefits were replaced with digital credits through the LifeSG mobile app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Since 2021, we have replaced cash and voucher-based NS recognition benefits with digital credits disbursed through the LifeSG mobile app.

sections.label: NS55 credits usage
sections.summary: NS55 credits of $100 were given electronically to over a million NSmen, with 76% used or started and an average rating of 4.8 stars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: As part of the NS55 Recognition Package, $100 worth of credits were distributed electronically in July last year to more than a million NSmen past and present.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: When we checked in mid-February 2023, the 136,000 NSmen who had rated the NS55 redemption eService on LifeSG app had given it an average of 4.8 out of five stars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Over the past seven months, 76% of NSmen have started using or have already used their credits fully.

sections.label: Insurance coverage doubled
sections.summary: In January, Group Term Life and Group Personal Accident insurance coverage was doubled from $150,000 to $300,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: In January, we doubled the coverage for the Group Term Life and Group Personal Accident insurance, up from $150,000 to $300,000.

sections.label: SAF safety audits and ESIS
sections.summary: The SAF Inspector-General's Office completed its second audit cycle, finding safety systems robust, and the Enterprise Safety Information System was fully adopted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: The SAF Inspector-General's Office recently completed its second audit cycle across all SAF formations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: The audit findings show that the SAF's safety management systems remain robust despite the ramp-up of training over the past year following pandemic-related disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: I announced last year that the SAF was developing an Enterprise Safety Information System (ESIS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: It has been fully adopted in the SAF, allowing quick spreading of safety lessons and easy submission of near misses and incidents by personnel across all ranks.

sections.label: Exit Permit and NSRCC hub
sections.summary: From April, NSmen need an Exit Permit only for 12 months or more, and NSRCC will build a social and recreation hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: From April this year onwards, NSmen will only need to apply for an Exit Permit when they leave Singapore for 12 months or more, up from the current six months or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Second, in appreciation of the contributions of our national servicemen, the National Service Resort and Country Club (NSRCC) will be building a social and recreation hub that will come with chalets, sports facilities and other family-centric amenities.

sections.label: Total Defence Review priorities
sections.summary: The 2021 Total Defence Review identified two priorities: raising awareness of threats and giving Singaporeans more opportunities to propose and partner on initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Member Miss Rachel Ong asked about how MINDEF has followed up on our 2021 Total Defence Review.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Through our review, we have identified two key priorities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The first is to help Singaporeans become more aware about the threats and challenges for our society, which would serve as a stepping-stone towards understanding how they can contribute to tackling these challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The second is to give Singaporeans more opportunities to propose Total Defence initiatives and to partner the government to implement these initiatives.

sections.label: Total Defence Sandbox exercise
sections.summary: An SMU student proposal led to a Community Exercise with over 120 participants at Chua Chu Kang Community Club for Total Defence Day 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Through the Total Defence Sandbox, a group of Singapore Management University (SMU) students proposed to conduct a table-top simulation to engage post-secondary students on Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We saw the potential of this idea and brought together Government agencies, grassroots organisations, education institutions and businesses to develop a full-fledged Community Exercise involving over 120 participants, as part of the 2023 Total Defence Day Commemoration Event.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The exercise was conducted over two days in Chua Chu Kang Community Club, where members of the local community came together to draw up plans to prepare for and respond to disruptions of essential supplies.

sections.label: Digital and Intelligence Service Sentinel Programme
sections.summary: The DIS launched the Sentinel Programme to teach youths digital and cybersecurity skills, with plans to extend it to more students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Our fourth service, the Digital and Intelligence Service (DIS), launched the Sentinel Programme last year to equip youths with digital and cybersecurity skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The programme was carefully crafted to expose students to foundational skills, such as basic programming, cryptography and network forensics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We received strong student interest in the pilot programme, and are working with other agencies, such as the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), to offer the programme to students from all secondary schools, junior colleges, polytechnics and ITEs in the coming years.

sections.label: ACCORD NS engagement sessions
sections.summary: ACCORD co-organised NS engagement sessions for over 11,000 post-secondary students, and most said the sessions helped them prepare for NS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: ACCORD co-organised NS engagement sessions for over 11,000 students from post-secondary education institutions in the past year and most agreed that the sessions helped them better prepare for NS.

sections.label: SDC sustainability and Navy Museum
sections.summary: SDC is on track to become a net-zero energy building this year, and the Navy Museum will reopen mid-year after a gallery makeover.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Echoing the Singapore Green Plan 2030 and MINDEF's commitment to environmental sustainability, SDC is on track to achieve its ambitious sustainability target of becoming a net-zero energy building by this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Navy Museum is undergoing a complete makeover of its galleries and will reopen to the public in the middle of the year.

sections.label: NS Gallery at Marina Bay
sections.summary: The NS Gallery at Marina Bay is being built within the new NS Square complex and remains on track to open by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The NS Gallery at Marina Bay is being built within the new NS Square complex and remains on track to open by 2027.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: The Speaker asks Mr Vikram Nair if he will withdraw his amendment, and he seeks leave to withdraw it.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: You have got lots of time, so you can go on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It looks like the House is supportive and it is being passed without clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
